correctness.rationale: The bihomogeneous graph map is induced by A=xy²t,B=xw²t,C=yzwt,D=z²wt. In the actual X=D=1 torus chart, equations give Y=CZ, W=BZ² and C²=ABZ²; elimination closure is the irreducible hypersurface R=k[Z,A,B,C]/(C²−ABZ²), independently checked by solving the birational monomial ratios and reviewing exact Groebner script. Element T=C/Z is integral (T²=AB) but T∉R: modulo Z the class C is nonzero in k[A,B,C]/(C²). S=k[Z,A,B,T]/(T²−AB) is finite birational normal (hypersurface S2, singular V(A,B,T) codim2), hence normalization. The conductor ideal is (Z,C): ZT=C and CT=ZAB lie in R; modulo Z the image R/(Z,C)=k[A,B] cannot contain f(A,B)T unless f=0. Jacobian of C²−ABZ² gives V(Z,C)∪V(A,B,C), with the latter normal A1-transverse away from Z=0. The former is height one and is exactly the chart nonnormal locus. Proof needs characteristic zero for this Jacobian description; it does not assert global conductor classification.
